integration_baseline_parity.why_four_surfaces: equal final equity is the weakest of the four and the easiest to hit by accident; guide 13.6 lists it among the parity claims that may not be made on their own

inert_hook_parity.why_three_runs: DISABLED never consults the hooks; INERT consults them and they decline. If those two paths differ, the act of asking has a side effect -- and a side effect that small would not read as a bug, it would read as an edge

cases.description: a 30% gap on the fill bar
a bar touching both the stop and the take profit
random walk with a technical exit
same tape with fees and slippage enabled

fill_trace_parity.detail: The rust backend returns an empty fill sequence at every report level tried (standard and full, with and without audit_detail_limit), so a fill-by-fill comparison is not available on this install. The ACCOUNT trace — equity, positions, fees, funding — is compared exactly and matches. Recorded as a blocked capability rather than described as full-trace parity (guide L02.8).

engine_fixed_intent_parity.claim_boundary: This establishes account-trace parity between two implementations of one contract. It is NOT a claim of Rust parity from final equity alone: every bar of equity, position, fee and funding is compared, and the missing fill-level trace is disclosed.

benchmark.rule: latency = measured seconds per fit x ceil(fits / workers). Partial waves round UP: three fits on two workers occupy two waves, and rounding down would hand the dynamic policy compute the resource budget forbids

training_account_contract.rule: training evaluations reset so candidates are comparable; the deployment account never resets. They are different contracts and a result from one is not a result from the other (guide 10.3)

training_jobs.isolation_rule: this runner never receives the deployment account, so a refit cannot mutate it. Candidate evaluation uses the training contract above, whose reset semantics are deliberately different from deployment (guide 10.3)

continuous_account.contract: ONE chronological sweep and ONE engine run over the whole window. The active parameter version changes at activation boundaries; the account does not restart, and no segment's equity comes from a separate run (T56, guide 10.3)

events.ordering_key: (available_at, causal rank of the kind, arrival sequence)
events.tie_break_rule: events sharing a timestamp are ordered by what causes what and then by arrival sequence. Millisecond equality is never used as an ordering (guide 4.2)
events.visibility_rule: a consumer at time t sees exactly the events whose available_at <= t. observed_at orders the world; available_at decides what may be acted on

segments.reporting_clock: daily UTC on one evaluation interval, unchanged by segmentation
segments.end_rule: a segment's end is written only when the NEXT activation exists. While it runs its end is null, because its length does not yet exist (guide L07.5)

activation_end_guard.rule: an activation is published with a start and no end. The end is written only when a LATER activation exists, and it is written to the segment record, never back onto the event the engine reads (guide L07.2, L07.5)

replay_parity.rule: feeding one event per step must equal the offline replay of the same tape under the same availability, or an offline result is not a claim about anything that could have run live (guide L07.7)

prefix_stability.rule: the account carries an open position across the cutoff, so this is the run where a leak would actually show: replacing every price after the cutoff must leave the equity and the active version bit-identical before it

records.explanation: no regime observation is available at all -> hold the incumbent

detail.why: no regime observation available at this decision time

records.explanation: an observation exists but is older than its TTL -> hold the incumbent

detail.why: observation is 2 days 00:00:00 old, past its TTL of 0 days 08:00:00

records.explanation: the refit did not converge or errored -> keep the previous model
a probe panel is short -> incomplete EVIDENCE, not bad performance
a job reported ready out of sequence -> activation still waits for READY
the engine refused an order -> recorded, position unchanged
the engine liquidated -> recorded as a real economic event, never masked
a worker died -> committed trials survive, uncommitted work is lost
an artifact write did not complete -> the artifact is unreadable

failures.rule: every failure resolves to the validated incumbent or a named incomplete status. No failure is resolved by choosing different parameters, and none is resolved by inventing a value (guide L07.6)
